sections.label: Combining PS(O)A and MCRBA
sections.summary: The Bill combines the PS(O)A and MCRBA into a single Payment Services Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill combines the PS(O)A and MCRBA into a single Payment Services Act.

sections.label: Seven payment service types
sections.summary: The services can be grouped into seven types, including account issuance, money transfers, merchant acquisition, e-money issuance, digital payment token dealing and exchanges, and money changing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The services can be grouped into seven types: account issuance, domestic money transfers, cross-border money transfers, merchant acquisition, e-money issuance, digital payment token dealing and exchanges, and money changing.

sections.label: Three licensee categories
sections.summary: A licensee may be a money-changing licensee, a standard payment institution, or a major payment institution.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: A licensee may be (a) a money-changing licensee, (b) a standard payment institution, or (c) a major payment institution.

sections.label: Standard payment institution services
sections.summary: Standard payment institutions may provide any combination of the seven defined payment services but below specified transaction flows or e-money float thresholds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Second, standard payment institutions may provide any combination of the seven defined payment services but below specified transaction flows or e-money float thresholds.

sections.label: Services MAS will regulate
sections.summary: Services that MAS will now be regulating are domestic money transfers, merchant acquisition, and digital payment token services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Services that MAS will now be regulating are domestic money transfers, merchant acquisition, and digital payment token (DPT) services.

sections.label: DPT AML/CFT requirements
sections.summary: Under the Bill, all providers of DPT dealing or exchange services in Singapore will have to meet AML/CFT requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Under the Bill, all providers of DPT dealing or exchange services in Singapore will have to meet anti-money laundering and counter financing of terrorism (AML/CFT) requirements.

sections.label: Safeguarding customer monies
sections.summary: The Bill requires major payment institutions to safeguard customer monies from insolvency loss by bank guarantee, trust account deposit, or other prescribed manner.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill requires major payment institutions to safeguard customer monies from loss through the institutions’ insolvency using any of the following means: first, an undertaking or guarantee by any bank in Singapore or prescribed financial institution to be fully liable to the customer for such monies; two, a deposit in a trust account; or three, safeguarding in such other manner as may be prescribed by MAS.

sections.label: MAS powers over payment systems
sections.summary: The Bill gives MAS powers to mandate third-party access, common platform participation, common standards, and technology and cybersecurity risk management requirements.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill will provide MAS with the powers to mandate the following outcomes: one, a designated payment system operator or major payment institution must allow third parties to access any payment system it operates, and the access regime imposed must be fair and not discriminatory; two, a major payment institution must participate in a specified common platform or equivalent arrangement to achieve interoperability of payment accounts; and three, a major payment institution must adopt a common standard to make widely-used payment acceptance methods interoperable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Bill will give MAS powers to impose technology risk management requirements, including cybersecurity risk management requirements, on all licensees.

sections.label: E-money issuers on-lending ban
sections.summary: E-money issuers will not be allowed to on-lend customer money or use it to materially finance their own business activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Accordingly, e-money issuers will not be allowed to on-lend any customer money or use any customer money to materially finance their own business activities.

sections.label: Stock and flow caps
sections.summary: The stock and flow caps were calibrated with regard to consumer needs and industry practices and set initially at $5,000 and $30,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The stock and flow caps were calibrated with due regard to consumer needs and existing industry practices and will be set initially at $5,000 and $30,000 respectively.

sections.label: Caps and financial stability
sections.summary: The caps will ensure continued financial system stability by reducing the risk of significant outflows from bank deposits to non-bank e-money.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: More importantly, the caps will ensure continued stability of the financial system, by reducing the risk of significant outflows from banks deposits to non-bank e-money which can undermine the stability of our banks.

sections.label: Wider payment activities protection
sections.summary: Expanding regulated activities under the new Payment Services Bill assures merchants and consumers of better MAS protection across a wider range of payment activities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: By expanding the scope of regulated activities beyond existing facilities and services under the new Payment Services Bill, merchants and consumers can be assured of better protection from MAS across a wider range of payment activities.

sections.label: Firms seeking MAS help
sections.summary: The passage asks how many firms have asked for help and what MAS is doing to help them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: How many firms have asked for help and what is MAS doing to help them?

sections.label: Safeguarding payment institution customer monies
sections.summary: The Minister said major payment institutions must safeguard customer monies via a bank undertaking or guarantee, or a trust account deposit.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The Minister mentioned in his speech that major payment institutions are required to safeguard their customers' monies through an undertaking or guarantee by any bank in Singapore or prescribed financial institution to be fully liable to the customer for such monies or have a deposit in a trust account.

sections.label: Limiting e-money to small transactions
sections.summary: The passage says limiting e-money to smaller day-to-day transactions is wise, noting personal stored-value caps of $5,000 and $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Despite the proliferation of online services, it would still be wise to limit the use of e-money to the smaller day-to-day transactions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: I note that the prescribed cap on personal stored-value balances is kept at $5,000 and $30,000 respectively for stock and flow caps respectively.

sections.label: Transferwise and Revolut objections
sections.summary: Transferwise and Revolut raised objections, saying their business models would be affected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Transferwise and Revolut outright raised objections, saying that their business models would be affected.

sections.label: Transferwise document requirement above US$10,000
sections.summary: Transferwise requires further documents for sending amounts of more than US$10,000 and above, in line with international wire regulations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Transferwise, for example, requires the provision of further document for sending amounts of more than US$10,000 and above, in line with international wire regulations.

sections.label: Exceptions or revised e-payment caps
sections.summary: The passage asks whether there are plans to make exceptions for certain e-payment platforms or revise the caps regularly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Are there plans to make exceptions for certain e-payment platforms, or revise the caps on a regular frequency to reflect the growing extent of e-money usage for major transactions in the near future?

sections.label: Payment Services Bill licensing virtual currencies
sections.summary: The Payment Services Bill consolidates payment services regulation, clarifies and increases consumer protections, and the question asks if virtual currencies will be licensed under it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Are there plans to license these virtual currencies under the Bill in future as well?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Payment Services Bill that is now up for Second Reading is an attempt to consolidate the regulation of payment services, which had previously been under two separate Acts, while clarifying and increasing protections for consumers in order to encourage and sufficiently regulate electronic payments.

sections.label: Transitional timeframe for licence threshold breach
sections.summary: The question asks what transitional timeframe a licensee gets when it only realises after the fact that its average monthly float breached the $3 million and $6 million thresholds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, in relation to the Bill's provision that a licensee would need to move from a standard to a major licence if the average monthly float over the previous calendar year exceeds $3 million and $6 million respectively for different sets of activities, what is the transitional timeframe given to the company, since it will only realise that it has breached the threshold after the breach has occurred, as it were?

sections.label: Bill bans cash withdrawals from stored-value balances
sections.summary: The Bill bans cash withdrawals from stored-value balances for AML and combating the financing of terrorism risk reasons.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Fourthly, Sir, the Bill bans cash withdrawals from stored-value balances for reasons of AML and combating the financing of terrorism (CFT) risk.

sections.label: MAS response on virtual currency and e-wallet caps
sections.summary: MAS says public virtual currency use is not yet significant enough for user protection, and that e-wallet caps limit customers' potential loss since e-money lacks deposit insurance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The MAS consultation paper response opines that the public use of virtual currency is not yet significant enough to warrant a need for user protection, going on to state that amendments to payment services legislation may be needed in future to respond to changes in the fast-developing world-wide virtual currency and virtual currency regulation space.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Lastly, Sir, I would like to query the e-wallet size restriction of $5,000 and transaction flow cap of $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is noted that five respondents to the MAS consultation paper felt that these caps would slow the growth of the e-payments industry while three additional respondents felt that the caps were set too low, and two respondents wanted better clarity on the rationale for imposing caps.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The MAS response to this feedback was that the caps were set at those levels to limit the customers' potential loss since e-money is not protected by deposit insurance.

sections.label: Raising caps with acknowledged risk warnings
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Government would consider raising the caps case-by-case if customers acknowledged sufficiently strong, concise and plainly worded risk warnings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Would the Government consider raising the caps on a case-by-case basis if sufficiently strong, concise and plainly worded risk warnings were given to customers, which customers were required to acknowledge?

sections.label: Bill regulates e-money and e-wallet safeguards
sections.summary: The Bill regulates e-money issuance so e-wallet funds are protected by legislation, and personal e-wallets get additional safeguards through e-wallet and transfer limits.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Specifically, the Bill will regulate the issuance of e-money, so that the funds we have in our e-wallets, including those for peer-to-peer transfers, will be protected by legislation.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Personal e-wallets will also receive additional safeguards in the form of e-wallet and transfer limits, thereby according greater protection to vulnerable users, such as the elderly.

sections.label: KPMG study on cash use
sections.summary: An MAS-commissioned KPMG study in 2016 found cash is used in 60% of all non-stored value facility transactions.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: An MAS-commissioned KPMG study in 2016 found that cash is used in 60% of all non-stored value facility transactions.

sections.label: KPMG study on cash and cheque costs
sections.summary: The same KPMG study estimated processing cash and cheques costs S$2 billion per year, around 0.5% of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The same KPMG study estimated that processing cash and cheques in terms of their storage, transportation, security and incineration costs S$2 billion per year or around 0.5% of our gross domestic product (GDP).

sections.label: Public education on e-payment options
sections.summary: The speaker proposes stepped-up public education on e-payment options, protections and incentives, especially targeted at the elderly.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Also, with the burgeoning market in e-payment providers out there, some consumers are clearly experiencing cognitive overload and perhaps even choice paralysis.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I would like to propose to the Minister that public education efforts be stepped up to better communicate to consumers the various options, protections and incentives that they enjoy with the different emerging e-payment methods out there.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, I would especially welcome targeted education for the elderly who are less well-acquainted with digital devices and platforms and may, therefore, be especially anxious about our shift towards a cashless society.

sections.label: Consumer protection provisions in Bill
sections.summary: The consumer protection provisions in the Bill will help boost consumer confidence.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The consumer protection provisions in the Bill will help boost consumer confidence.

sections.label: Support for the Bill
sections.summary: The speaker states that, notwithstanding the issues raised, he supports this Bill.

sentences.speaker: Prof Lim Sun Sun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: (In English): In conclusion, Mr Speaker, notwithstanding the issues I have raised, I support this Bill.

sections.label: Section 20 credit services prohibition
sections.summary: Section 20 prohibits payment services licensees from offering credit services.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Section 20 prohibits payment services licensees from offering credit services.

sections.label: MAS Sandbox credit facilities trial
sections.summary: Asks whether regulatory flexibility, perhaps via the MAS Sandbox, allows payment services firms to trial innovations including credit facilities with safeguards.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Being able to trial such services in Singapore could be useful.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I wish to ask if we have sufficient regulatory flexibility, perhaps through the MAS Sandbox, to allow payment services firms to trial innovations that may include credit facilities, with appropriate safeguards.

sections.label: E-money competitiveness and customer funds
sections.summary: Asks whether payment services licensees may invest customer funds in liquid, low-risk instruments like Government securities to manage cost of capital.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We should be careful to avoid making e-money services less competitive than alternatives, such as direct transfers from deposit accounts or credit facilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I wish to ask if, in practice, payment services licensees will be allowed to reduce or manage the cost of capital by investing customer funds in liquid, low-risk instruments, such as Government securities.

sections.label: Interoperability and access regime enforcement
sections.summary: Asks what market tests, thresholds or behaviours MAS could construe as requiring enforcement of the Bill's interoperability and access provisions.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Payment Services Bill will allow for mandated interoperability and an access regime, which can ensure that networks are not abused to stifle competition and innovation.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I wish to ask if the Minister could discuss what types of market tests, thresholds or other behaviours could be construed by MAS as requiring enforcement of these provisions.

sections.label: Fit and Proper criteria for fintech
sections.summary: Seeks assurance that MAS will consider fintech entrepreneurs' technology backgrounds when applying Fit and Proper criteria, so firms compete fairly.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Many fintech firms are headed by entrepreneurs with technology backgrounds rather than financial backgrounds.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It will be useful if the Minister could assure the fintech industry that MAS will take these concerns into account when applying the Fit and Proper criteria.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is important to ensure that both fintech firms and traditional financial institutions can compete fairly to deliver innovation and growth for all Singaporeans.

sections.label: Prescribed annual licence fees guidelines
sections.summary: Asks whether guidelines exist yet for the prescribed annual fees for the three classes of licences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Are there any guidelines as yet for the prescribed annual fees for the three classes of licences?

sections.label: Missing Annexure B virtual currencies
sections.summary: Notes that Annexure B, referred to in the Bill for definitions of virtual currencies, is not found in the proposed Bill document.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It refers to an Annexure B in the Bill for definitions of "virtual currencies".

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, the Annexure is not to be found in the proposed Bill document.

sections.label: Cashing out e-money from banks
sections.summary: A speaker says the Bill appears to prohibit cashing out e-money from a bank e-wallet a year later.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, if the licensee is a bank, when I open an e-wallet with a bank and then one year later I want to cash that e-money back out, the provision in this part of the Bill seems to be trying to prohibit me from doing just that.

sections.label: Proposed Bill for digital businesses
sections.summary: A speaker asks whether another proposed Bill would cover e-money, e-wallets and virtual currencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Is there another proposed Bill to cover such businesses in the digital age that would encompass e-money, e-wallets and virtual currencies and so on?

sections.label: Willingness to try innovation
sections.summary: The passage states innovation may fail, and that caution would undermine the innovative spirit and national culture of innovation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, the very essence of innovation means much of the innovation may not succeed in the end.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We need to be willing to try, to change as we go along, and even to abandon what we started off with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Mohamed Irshad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: If we are too cautious, we would undermine the innovative spirit itself and fail to promote a widespread national culture of innovation so necessary to propel Singapore ahead.

sections.label: Migrant worker remittances from Singapore
sections.summary: A World Bank Report of April 2018 states migrant workers in Singapore sent at least US$5.6 billion to the top five remittance destinations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a World Bank Report published in April 2018, migrant workers in Singapore sent a grand total of at least US$5.6 billion in remittances to the top five remittance destination countries alone.

sections.label: Cash pay and remittance charges
sections.summary: A KPMG report says 75% of foreign domestic workers are paid in cash and remittance agencies charge $5 to $12 per transaction.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to a report by KPMG, 75% of foreign domestic workers are paid in cash.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In addition, remittance agencies charge $5 to $12 for every transaction.

sections.label: Electronic salary payment requirements
sections.summary: Employers of S Pass holders earning $2,200 and above must pay salaries electronically, but this is not extended to Work Permit holders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Employers of S Pass holders – those earning $2,200 and above per month – are required to pay their salaries through electronic means, but this requirement is not extended to the one million employees who are Work Permit holders, a lower wage category.

sections.label: Including migrant workers in Bill
sections.summary: It states that including migrant workers in the Bill's implementation is a responsibility and opportunity, through legislation and education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It connects migrant workers to their families, gives them a sense of purpose for their struggles and, in some ways, empowers them to have dreams and aspirations for a better life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is, therefore, a responsibility and opportunity for us to include them in the implementation of this Bill with legislation and education.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: After all, we know that the way forward for us as a Smart Nation goes beyond just the best laws and the latest payment technologies; it is how we stay human and inclusive.

sections.label: Licence requirement for payment services
sections.summary: Section 5(1) prohibits providing any type of payment services in Singapore without a licence, if a licence is required.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Section 5(1) prohibits any person from providing any type of payment services in Singapore without a licence, if a licence is required.

sections.label: Enforcement against non-Singapore businesses
sections.summary: It asks the Minister to clarify how the provisions will be enforced against non-Singapore businesses that do not operate in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister clarify how it intends to enforce these provisions against non-Singapore businesses that do not operate in Singapore?

sections.label: ICOs in Singapore and scams
sections.summary: It cites ICObench that Singapore has 524 ICOs raising US$2.1 billion, and Statis Group that 80% of 2017 ICOs were scams.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Based on a report by ICObench, an authoritative rating body, Singapore has the second highest number of ICOs on ICObench’s platform, with 524 ICOs launched and US$2.1 billion raised.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: While platforms that issue digital tokens will be regulated under the proposed regime, those within the industry have expressed concerns to me that there should be greater regulatory oversight over businesses that operate on those platforms and raise funds by offering ICOs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to a report by ICO advisory firm Statis Group, 80% ICOs in 2017 were scams.

sections.label: Registering ICO businesses with MAS
sections.summary: It proposes that all businesses that conduct an ICO must register themselves with MAS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: First, I propose that all businesses that conduct an ICO must register themselves with MAS.

sections.label: MAS public campaigns on ICOs
sections.summary: It proposes that MAS could conduct public campaigns to raise awareness about ICOs, their potential windfalls and pitfalls.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Second, MAS could conduct public campaigns to raise awareness about ICOs, its potential windfalls and its pitfalls.

sections.label: Fraud and funds abuse penalties
sections.summary: The Minister is asked whether he would consider legislating to enforce penalties on fraud and funds abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Would the Minister consider legislating to enforce penalties on fraud and funds abuse?

sections.label: Reorganised payment services licensing
sections.summary: The Bill reorganises these services as account issuance, e-money issuance, cross-border money transfer and money-changing under a new activity-based licensing regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: The Bill will reorganise these services as account issuance service, e-money issuance service, cross-border money transfer service, and money-changing service under a new activity-based licensing regime.

sections.label: Two payment regulatory frameworks
sections.summary: The Bill has a designation regime for systemically important payment systems and a licensing regime for retail payment services, including domestic transfers, merchant acquisition and digital payment tokens.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: The Bill comprises two parallel regulatory frameworks: (a) a designation regime that enables MAS to regulate systemically important payment systems for financial stability and efficiency reasons, and (b) a licensing regime that focuses on retail payment services facing consumers and merchants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: The latter encompasses a wide range of new payment activities, which include domestic money transfers, merchant acquisition and the purchase and sale of digital payment tokens.

sections.label: Risk mitigating provisions
sections.summary: Key risk mitigating provisions include interoperability powers to reduce fragmentation and powers to impose risk-mitigating measures for ML/TF purposes under the MAS Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
sentences.text: Key risk mitigating provisions include interoperability powers which MAS may exercise where necessary to reduce fragmentation of widely-used payment solutions, and the power to impose risk-mitigating measures for ML/TF purposes under the MAS Act (Cap 186).

sections.label: Protection of customer monies
sections.summary: Major payment institutions are required under the Bill to protect customer monies under prescribed methods if they go insolvent.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about how customer monies are protected by payment service providers if they go insolvent and I have explained in my speech that major payment institutions are required under the Bill to protect customer monies under prescribed methods.

sections.label: Regulating cryptocurrency services approach
sections.summary: The intent is to regulate DPT services only for ML/TF risks, and not for customer protection at the moment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Mr Leon Perera also asked about the approach and timeframe for regulating cryptocurrency services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: I had explained in my speech that our intent currently is to regulate DPT services only for ML/TF risks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: This is because the use of DPTs in Singapore is low compared to countries like the US, Japan and South Korea.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, at the moment, we do not intend to regulate DPT services for customer protection.

sections.label: Electronic salary payment for migrant workers
sections.summary: MOM is consulting stakeholders on possibly mandating electronic salary payment for migrant workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: MOM is currently consulting stakeholders on the option of mandating electronic salary payment for migrant workers.

sections.label: Bill compared to other financial centres
sections.summary: The Bill resembles frameworks in Australia, Hong Kong and the UK but covers four identified payments risks in one legislation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Bill contains similar aspects to regulatory frameworks in other financial centres, such as Australia, Hong Kong and the UK.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: What this Bill sets itself apart from other jurisdictions is that it comprehensively covers four risks identified in the payments landscape in a single legislation.

sections.label: Licence class thresholds set in Bill
sections.summary: Given certainty for licence applicants and licensees, the licence class determining thresholds are set out in the Bill itself.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: On balance, weighing this, and this being a new Bill, we err on the side of giving certainty to licence applicants and licensees, and set out the licence class determining thresholds in the Bill itself.

sections.label: Calibration of $5,000 and $30,000 thresholds
sections.summary: The $5,000 and $30,000 figures were calibrated after considering a few considerations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As to why they are set at $5,000 and $30,000, these were calibrated after, in view of a few considerations.

sections.label: Licensing and local presence requirements
sections.summary: Payment service providers in Singapore need a licence unless exempted, with local presence and an executive director meeting stated criteria.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Anyone carrying on a business providing payment services in Singapore needs to hold a licence under the Bill, unless it is exempted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: The Bill requires all licensees, local and foreign – and foreign to have local presence, that is, to have a physical place of business or registered office in Singapore where customers can seek redress and where MAS can access the licensee's books.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Further, licensees must have at least one executive director who is a Singapore Citizen, a Permanent Resident or a person in a prescribed class.

sections.label: Prohibition due to prudential stability considerations
sections.summary: Because of prudential and financial stability considerations, such activities were prohibited as high thresholds could cause deposit and cash liquidity outflow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If you set too high, it can potentially also lead to a significant outflow of deposit and cash liquidity out of the banking system.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: So, because of all these prudential and stability considerations for our financial system, we prohibited such activities.

sections.label: Singapore payments market competition approach
sections.summary: Singapore is susceptible to one provider dominating a market, so it deliberately took a different approach to allow more competition and innovation in payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As a small market, Singapore is especially susceptible to one provider dominating a market and abusing their position.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: We have, therefore, deliberately taken a different approach so as to allow more competition and innovation in the payments space.

sections.label: FAST PayNow SGQR interoperability initiatives
sections.summary: Initiatives such as FAST, PayNow, unified point-of-sale and SGQR serve to achieve interoperability, convenience and ease of use.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: As I have explained in my Second Reading speech, initiatives, such as FAST, PayNow, unified point-of-sale, SGQR, they serve to achieve interoperability, convenience and ease of use.

sections.label: Non-banks in FAST system
sections.summary: Non-banks are being accepted into the Fast And Secure Transfers system and a workgroup is ongoing to discuss this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: Another thing that we are doing is to accept non-banks into the Fast And Secure Transfers (FAST) system and a workgroup is ongoing to discuss this.

sections.label: Motion moved and Sitting suspended
sections.summary: The member begged to move, suspended the Sitting and would take the Chair at 4.50 pm, with the Sitting suspended at 4.33 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: With that, Mr Deputy Speaker, I beg to move.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: I suspend the Sitting and will take the Chair at 4.50 pm.

sentences.speaker: Mr Deputy Speaker
sentences.text: Sitting accordingly suspended  at 4.33 pm until 4.50 pm.
